item.title: U of T Alumni Day at AFC Toronto - Soccer + CNE Access in One Ticket — Sun Aug 30, 3:00 PM — BMO Field
item.description:
Make the most of your summer with a high-energy afternoon of soccer, alumni connection, and one of Toronto’s biggest seasonal attractions – all in a single ticket. Join fellow U of T alumni, family and friends at BMO Field as AFC Toronto takes on the Ottawa Rapid in Northern Super League action – Canada’s top tier of women’s professional soccer. Your Alumni Day ticket includes:
Discounted ticket pricing for reserved U of T alumni seats in Section 119 Alumni shoutout on the stadium videoboard A U of T group photo on-site Complimentary general admission to the Canadian National Exhibition (CNE) – included with your match ticket
Why this even is a can’t miss: Your ticket doesn’t just get you into the match – it unlocks same-day admission to the CNE, giving you access to rides, games, food vendors and entertainment across the grounds before or after kick-off. It’s a complete summer outing in one experience. Event Details Date: Sunday, August 30, 2026 Location: BMO Field (170 Princes’

item.title: Cancelled - Leaders Choice: No-Drop Country Ride - Victoria Square to Goodwood via Vivian — Mon Aug 31, 9:00 AM
item.description:
CANCELLED FOR AUG 31 No-Drop Country Ride Annina's Bakery and Schitt's Creek Set Photo-Op Borrowing a popular Wednesday Wheelies route, we'll be starting north of the city, then we'll venture out to Annina's bakery. North up quiet country roads, then east along Vivian Rd, before turning south towards Musselman's Lake and Goodwood. We will be stopping for a snack/butter tart at Annina's and optional photo op at the Schitt's Creek set across the street before finishing the ride. If you have a TBN jersey, please wear it and show your club pride! This is a Tourist or advanced Urban Roller level ride, not because of the pace, but because of some hills. There will be regrouping at major turns. Eve...

item.title: Branch Art Exhibit: Works by Michael Kaplan — Tue Sep 1, 12:00 AM — Forest Hill
item.description: Throughout the month of September, works by artist Michael Sydney Kaplan will be on display at the Forest Hill branch. Michael was born and raised in Toronto, Ontario. At birth, he was given the nickname Mickey, and that has been with him ever since. His extended family includes a number of professional artists, actors, authors, and politicians. The arts are in his genes. At the age of 7 or 8, he was enrolled in painting classes at The Art Gallery of Ontario upon the insistence of his aunt, Chip Feldman, a professional artist herself. Since then, his artistic teachers and mentors have included Jay Dampf and Sam Kara at Dreams Studio, and currently, Gelen Golrokh at Art Wish. On his first trip to Paris in 1962, Mickey fell under the spell of the Impressionists. He loves the light, bright images and revealing brush strokes of Monet, Manet, and Pissarro, as demonstrated in his work. item.title: What is Artificial Intelligence? — Tue Sep 1, 2:00 PM — Ethennonnhawahstihnen'
item.description:
AI technologies have become increasingly prevalent in many aspects of modern life, including healthcare, finance, transportation, and entertainment. Some examples of AI applications include virtual assistants like Siri and Alexa, self-driving cars, fraud detection systems, and personalized recommendations in online shopping. Come join this beginner in-person class to learn what AI is, how it learns and predicts outcomes, considerations when using GenAI applications, and how the Internet of Things (IOT) applies to AI. item.title: 3D Design with Onshape — Thu Sep 3, 6:00 PM — Annette Street
item.description: Learn how to create parametric designs using cloud based software Onshape. This hands-on workshop introduces participants to the fundamentals of 3D design using Onshape, a cloud-based CAD software. Whether you're an aspiring engineer, designer, or hobbyist, this session provides the tools and knowledge to start creating your own 3D models. What You’ll Learn: Getting Started: Overview of Onshape's interface, navigation tools, and cloud-based collaboration features. Core Design Principles: Understanding 3D modeling basics, including sketches, extrusions, and revolutions. Hands-On Practice: Creating simple 3D parts, assembling components, and exploring design modifications. Best Practices: Tips for efficient modeling, managing design iterations, and exporting models for 3D printing or other applications. This program is ideal for beginners with no prior experience in CAD software, as well as those looking to explore Onshape's capabilities. Registration will start 2 weeks before this class

Source: Toronto Public Library — Teens
